feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital platform leadership and credible progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and scanability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression from coordinator to director, then consulting, which supports credibility and seniority.  
- Good use of scale and scope: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add impact.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a way that fits current digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across multiple sections; consolidate Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation varies in lists; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found, but the footer project block is too compressed and hurts readability.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper differentiation and one or two concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and reduce list-like phrasing; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Emphasize leadership outcomes, not just scope: modernization, governance, analytics, and AI should sound tied to organizational performance.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Led enterprise digital strategy for a 10,000+ page Drupal ecosystem serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics, editorial, multimedia, and AI-enabled search systems for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search systems.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered extensively in skills and experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and insight systems • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Clarify technical/strategic strengths without repeating tools: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration
- Refine sector language for precision: Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Keep multimedia concise and parallel: Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps with “Topline Skills”; consider using one for strategic themes and the other for tools/platforms only.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tighten wording, standardize style, and emphasize only the most distinctive examples.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and purpose.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Launched/Built/Developed…” and trim stacked descriptors.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent serial commas.
- Consider this tighter version: AI Hybrid Search: Launched an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery. We Are Counties Microsite: Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and modular components for future growth. Organization Anniversary Campaign: Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series: Produced a recurring advocacy video series across planning, production, and distribution for web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with Work Experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs if keeping all four items.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-led statements, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance practices across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaigns launched, workflow time saved, search success gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement” is broad and repeats the summary.
- CMS/front-end/troubleshooting may duplicate technical skills unless tied to a notable result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-value leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Prioritize the website transformation first and make it outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel language and add measurable outcomes if available: open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine analytics/governance bullets into one operational impact bullet if space is tight: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing publishing standards and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and scale.
- Video production/studio language may overlap with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize building the in-house studio as the leadership-level differentiator.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program rather than launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than restating broad communications capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level language tied to current positioning.
- Prioritize enterprise leadership and governance over broad “messaging” language.
- Keep to 4 concise bullets max; use parallel phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector audience strategy and advocacy content planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies section.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider dropping “messaging” unless paired with a clearer differentiator like audience strategy or governance.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Consider dropping older/lower-priority platforms here (e.g., WordPress, SharePoint) unless they are central to target roles; keep them in “Technical + IT.”
- Replace “Power Pages” with it only if actively used in recent roles; otherwise it weakens the recency signal.
- If space allows, sharpen with impact language: “Drupal platform delivery,” “enterprise CMS modernization,” or “search and discovery systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats the header/core competencies; keep it here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & performance optimization.”
- Use grouped, higher-signal wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace weaker items with more outcome-oriented language: swap “Leadership reporting” for “executive dashboards and decision support”; consider “measurement strategy and KPI design” instead of just “KPI design.”

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Hybrid and virtual event production

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and slightly dated versus the more strategic, recent emphasis elsewhere. Tighten it to reflect higher-level production capability and the in-house studio/buildout impact shown in recent roles.

- Replace with more specific, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”

- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad categories (“studio operations”) with vague formats (“livestreaming”) without qualifiers

- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; consider keeping the Topline Skills version more technical/specific

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should stay concise and emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level/use: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider trimming lower-signal tools if this section feels crowded: remove **GitHub Pages** unless it supports portfolio or lightweight site publishing relevant to target roles.
- Keep formatting parallel with other technical items; avoid turning this into a second “web strategy” section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is redundant with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists the same core platforms plus modernization work.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in **Core Competencies**, so avoid adding broader descriptors here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place last or label as legacy: **JavaScript (including legacy jQuery)**
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g. **front-end implementation for Drupal-based public web properties** or **deployment/workflow automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed stack here and shortening/removing the overlapping topline line.
- **API integrations** and **workflow automation** are also echoed elsewhere; avoid repeating both in multiple sections unless phrased differently.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful, but it currently reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by separating true automation platforms from project/collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Rewrite as: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop **Basecamp** unless it was used recently or materially in current/Director-level work.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers only where strongest: **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project tracking)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with **“Workflow automation”** and **“Airtable systems”** in Topline Skills; keep this version tool-focused and let Topline Skills carry the strategic framing.
- **Slack** and **Teams** are common collaboration tools; include them only if they support a broader workflow/operations story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and audience engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of only listing tools: **campaign automation, newsletter distribution, segmentation, and member communications**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp; campaign automation, audience segmentation, newsletter operations, and member engagement communications**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad email/newsletter management already covered in **Director of Digital Media** and **Associate Communications Director**.
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider naming the strongest one in a recent experience bullet and keeping this skills line shorter.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a sharper capabilities list or add specificity that supports recent analytics leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and group for scanability: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace broad terms with more concrete ones: swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis**; swap **Dashboarding** for **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards**
- If truthful, add one higher-signal capability instead of a generic term: **conversion analysis**, **tagging/measurement strategy**, or **behavior analytics**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and leaving strategic capabilities there.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same framing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify scope: mention key channels once, then focus on 2–3 distinct contributions such as website refresh support, livestream production, and weekly video series execution.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of livestreams/events supported, frequency/volume of video content, audience growth, or workflow improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows. Provided informal supervision and training for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; keep this more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases that don’t add distinct value.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the clearest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the digital support language: replace “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or how the podcast supported member engagement/policy communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid framing this as broad digital leadership; later NACo roles already cover web, video, and channel management more strongly.
- “Multimedia production” is repeated elsewhere—use “first podcast” to keep this item distinct.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it into clearer tool categories will improve scanability, and some items overlap with stronger multimedia claims already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Split tools from capabilities; keep this item software-focused where possible.
